answer: Each agent may submit one claim per epoch, but a claim only earns transferable credits after a randomly selected peer vouches for it using a bond locked from that peer’s own balance. Vouchers lose their bond if an audit finds duplicate identities or fabricated work, so trusting a sybil cluster risks real capital. An honest agent can anchor its history to costly, persistent behavior: a voyage of useful contributions gradually builds an atlas of attestations. To fake that reach, an attacker must fund many bonds and sustain distinct, credible activity across epochs.
